recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce not-done or stopped for FHIR-13881; future Pharmacy changes to MedicationDispense status semantics should be handled through a new or already-final later issue such as the FHIR-40692 family.
issue_request: FHIR-13881 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Pharmacy change request for STU3 MedicationDispense. It asked to clean up the status definitions around dispense phases and patient pickup, and the final resolution required applying the follow-up definitions and renaming Not-Done to Cancelled.
initial_application: The Jira snapshot records application on 2018-02-16 in git-svn commit e4206a3abafba1275c89a32c29f2715a17e0e0e7. That commit changed the then-authoritative MedicationDispense spreadsheet so MedicationDispense.status was required, the short status list used cancelled instead of not-done, and the status code definitions for in-progress, cancelled, on-hold, and completed matched the follow-up comments. Later source refactors moved this terminology into the current source/medicationdispense CodeSystem and related conformance files.
additional_context: MedicationDispense is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/medicationdispense terminology, StructureDefinition, examples, and source/status-codes.xml are current build inputs. A later Applied Pharmacy issue, FHIR-40692, intentionally changed the old stopped status to unfulfilled and refined related status wording for R6; that issue is already represented on the combined branch by commit 79ecb41f09ac5a4869795f7fca29481c6613e938, so it was not re-decided or reversed here. No Confluence references for FHIR-13881 and no directly relevant Zulip discussion were found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current MedicationDispense status CodeSystem already uses cancelled, defines in-progress as ready for pickup, cancelled as not and never picked up by the patient, on-hold as waiting for an external reactivation event, and completed as picked up. The current StructureDefinition short text and status-codes table align with later unfulfilled/declined current status semantics rather than the old not-done/stopped wording.
